topic: REVLab Review 2026: Windows PE Reverse Engineering Workflow Platform

key_points: REVLab is a Windows PE reverse engineering workflow platform (Python 3.11 + FastAPI + SQLite)
Covers static analysis, packer detection (30+ signatures), unpacking, disassembly (Capstone), decompile (Ghidra Headless), dynamic sandbox (VMware), network capture (pktmon + custom pcap parsing)
Embedded Vue Flow graph-based workflow canvas v3 with conditional branches, approval nodes, failure policies (retry/skip/abort), and variable system ({{var}} references)
Built-in MCP Server with 37 tools to integrate Codex / Claude Code / Cursor / custom AI agents; external AI can fully drive workflows via MCP
Three workflow templates: general PE full-auto, UE (Unreal Engine) special, and Unity engine special (IL2CPP metadata analysis + SDK dump)

AI assist nodes (pe_ai_assist / ue_ai_assist / unity_ai_assist) combine prior node evidence for conclusions and can search the web for packer signatures, DLL/function purposes, and suspicious behavior patterns
AI workbench: multi-session persistence, context compression, session-level model and thinking strength selection
Model presets: OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Zhipu, Kimi, SiliconFlow, Gemini, OpenRouter, Groq, Together, Mistral, Perplexity, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic-compatible proxy, Ollama, LM Studio
Fingerprint hashing: MD5/SHA1/SHA256/SHA512, imphash, ssdeep
PE parsing with pefile + LIEF dual-engine cross-validation, Shannon entropy on sections, Rich Header, PDB clues, digital signature verification, TLS callbacks
MIT license; local-only processing with no external requests unless explicitly triggered
Setup via setup.ps1 with -All flag to auto-install Python/Node/Java 21, download Ghidra and optional PE tools
Agent-native reverse-engineering lab with a 197-article knowledge base
Provides MCP tools and CTF/APK/PE automation workflows
~1046 GitHub stars, 257 forks (as of Aug 2026), actively maintained
Positions itself around agent-native workflows with a large embedded knowledge base
Open-source AI reverse-engineering agent using Ghidra and LLMs
Reconstructs and validates C/C++ functions from binaries
~1330 GitHub stars; focus is on AI-assisted function reconstruction rather than full workflow platform
Windows-based AI-powered reverse engineering toolkit (AIO)
Built for security, malware analysis, pentesting, and educational purposes
~343 GitHub stars; broader pentesting scope rather than dedicated PE workflow platform
AV-TEST reports about 450,000 new malicious programs (malware) and potentially unwanted applications (PUA) registered per month
Underscores the scale of new binaries analysts must process, motivating automated workflow tooling
SMBs faced over 6 million unique threat instances in first half of 2025 (N-able 2025 Annual Threat Report)

stats.fact: AV-TEST registers about 450,000 new malicious programs (malware) and potentially unwanted applications (PUA) per month
SMBs faced over 6 million unique threat instances in just the first half of 2025 (January-June), per N-able's 2025 Annual Threat Report
REVLab offers 30+ packer detection signatures covering UPX, ASPack, PECompact, Petite, MPRESS, VMProtect, Themida, Armadillo, and more

REVLab ships an MCP Server exposing 37 tools for AI-agent integration (analyze_pe, disassemble, detect_packer, unpack_known, decompile_ghidra, run_dynamic, capture_network, wf_* workflow control, wf_resolve_ai, etc.)
REVLab uses dual-engine PE parsing with pefile + LIEF for cross-validation
REVLab disassembly is powered by Capstone (x86/x64); decompilation uses Ghidra Headless requiring Java 21
open-reverselab (agent-native reverse-engineering lab) has ~1046 GitHub stars and 257 forks, with a 197-article knowledge base
auto-re-agent (AI reverse-engineering agent using Ghidra + LLMs) has ~1330 GitHub stars

angles: The 'all-in-one workflow platform' angle: REVLab consolidates static analysis, unpacking, disassembly, decompilation, dynamic sandboxing, and network capture into a single visual workflow canvas instead of stitching together separate CLI tools
The AI-agent-native angle: unique MCP integration (37 tools) lets Codex/Claude Code/Cursor fully drive the analysis pipeline, bridging human visual workflows and autonomous AI agents
The three-engine coverage angle: general PE + UE (Unreal Engine) + Unity engine specializations make it broader than most PE-only tools, appealing to game-security and malware analysts alike

The honesty angle: REVLab explicitly distinguishes 'confirmed / candidate / unconfirmed' static findings and does not mask unverified addresses as validated, addressing a common trust problem in AI-assisted RE
The compliance-first angle: clear legal disclaimers, lab-only use, and local-only processing make it safe to recommend
The 2026 relevance angle: with ~450k new malware samples/month and 6M SMB threat instances in H1 2025, automated pipeline tooling is increasingly necessary
